headline: Two Red Stripes Cut Bird Deaths at Wind Farm by 83%
meta_description: A simple paint job on wind turbine blades at South Africa's Hopefield wind farm dramatically reduced wildlife collisions.
summary_short: Painting two red stripes on a single blade of four turbines at South Africa's Hopefield wind farm led to an estimated 83% reduction in bird and bat deaths.
body:
Painting two red stripes on a single turbine blade may be the answer to a problem that has long troubled renewable energy: keeping wildlife safe around wind farms.

At South Africa's Hopefield wind farm, researchers tested this straightforward intervention on just four turbines. The results were striking—an estimated median 83% reduction in collisions. The simple visual marker appears to make spinning blades more visible to birds and bats, giving them crucial seconds to change course.

The finding suggests that wind power and wildlife protection aren't mutually exclusive. If this low-cost, easy-to-implement solution holds up under further study, it could be rolled out across farms worldwide, offering a path forward for clean energy that doesn't come at nature's expense.
quick_facts: Two red stripes painted on one turbine blade
